blindSummary:
This state/province — the national capital's metro area — carries the country's most developed protective legal framework at the local level, in a country with no national anti-discrimination statute covering gender identity. Its main city enacted a comprehensive 2025 SOGIESC anti-discrimination ordinance (revising a 2014 city gender-fair ordinance), and in July 2025 became the first local government unit in the country to enact a gender-inclusive health ordinance creating a framework for gender-affirming primary care and specialised services. For a visitor, these are the only enforceable protections available anywhere in the country — complaint routes to a city health office or the city gender desk that simply do not exist in sibling states/provinces.

Against that, two of the six documented killings of trans women in the 2024–2025 national series occurred here (a trans woman strangled during a drinking session in a capital satellite city, March 2024; a college-educated therapist known as "Christine" stabbed in a northern capital city in September 2025, for which two men were arrested), and a state college reportedly denied enrollment to trans women requiring short haircuts (March 2024 video). The national human-rights commission issued public statements condemning both the campus practice and the killings, and arrests followed in one of the cities.
blindSourceSummaries: City public notice: the 2025 ordinance 'providing for a comprehensive anti-discrimination policy on the basis of sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC)', revising the city's 2014 gender-fair ordinance; posted as the city council's 22nd ordinance with the full text downloadable.

City government press release: the city became the first local government unit in the country to enact a comprehensive gender-inclusive health ordinance (July 2025), introduced by city councillors, creating a framework for gender-affirming primary care, mental-health support and specialised medical services through the city public-health system; with a statement from the city's mayor.

Trans-murder memorial site report entry: a 29-year-old trans woman killed in a capital satellite city on 1 March 2024, category violence, cause strangled; the underlying report adds that she was killed during a drinking session.

Trans-murder memorial site report entry: a 44-year-old trans woman known as 'Christine', stabbed in a northern capital city on 22 September 2025; the underlying report adds she was a college-educated therapist found in a rented apartment after neighbours heard an argument, and two men were arrested.

Official statement by the national human-rights commission over the viral video of a transgender woman compelled to get a haircut as a condition for enrollment at a state college in the capital: the commission expresses deep concern, notes the 2021 student handbook requires male students to get a barber's haircut while complaints continue despite repeated joint discussions and demand letters from student groups, and urges an impartial investigation and a review of the code of conduct.
blindLocalsOnly: The gender-inclusive health ordinance's clinical services - gender-affirming primary care and mental-health support in city facilities - are what residents use; what a visitor can actually invoke is the anti-discrimination complaint machinery (the city gender desk and city health office routes).
